key_risks.description: Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow turned negative at $(7,604) million versus +$18,184 million a year earlier. Net property and equipment purchases rose to $169.0 billion, outpacing operating cash flow of $161.4 billion, and financing activities provided $75.2 billion to cover the gap.

Capex funding is shifting toward external capital. The company issued multiple large note offerings in 2026 (USD, EUR, CHF, CAD) and signed a $17.5 billion undrawn delayed-draw term loan. Interest expense rose to $1,314 million in Q2 2026 from $516 million, while total cash and marketable securities were flat at about $123 billion. Property and equipment acquired but not yet paid rose sharply (about $29.3 billion in the first half of 2026 versus $5.4 billion), a deferred cash outflow not yet in reported free cash flow.

Depreciation lag: AWS net additions to property and equipment were about $48.6 billion in Q2 2026 versus $16.0 billion a year earlier, while AWS depreciation and amortization rose only to about $8.1 billion from $4.8 billion. Assets not yet in service carry little depreciation, so reported AWS margins may not reflect the full cost of the build-out as it comes online.

Technology infrastructure and capex are expected to keep rising in 2026. Cash capex was $53.1 billion in Q2 2026 versus $31.4 billion and $96.3 billion for the six months versus $55.6 billion. Technology and infrastructure expense grew 22% in Q2 and 25% for the six months, and total commitments are reported at about $650 billion versus about $387 billion previously, reducing flexibility if demand softens.

AWS contracted backlog of about $496 billion (weighted-average remaining life 6.4 years) is concentrated in large AI-lab commitments: an OpenAI expansion of $100 billion over 8 years and an Anthropic expansion of more than $100 billion over 10 years, both including obligations tied to AWS chip performance. Recognition depends on customer usage and Amazon's performance, and the counterparties are partly funded by Amazon's own equity investments.

Earnings quality and valuation risk from non-operating items: Q2 2026 net income of $62.6 billion included $53.4 billion of Other income (expense), net against operating income of $27.5 billion. Private-company equity investments (including Anthropic and OpenAI) carried at $122.3 billion versus $16.2 billion at year-end, partly via Level 3 fair value adjustments recognized in other income, so results can swing with private-market valuations. Provision for income taxes rose to $18.2 billion.

Further funding obligations to AI-lab partners: subsequent to June 30, 2026, the remaining $21.3 billion Commitment Amount was invested in Series C Preferred Stock of OpenAI, adding to exposure whose maximum loss is generally limited to carrying value and future funding commitments.

bull_case: AWS growth accelerated to 37% in Q2 2026 ($42.2B of sales) from 17% a year earlier, and 33% for the first half, on a segment that is now 21% of net sales.

AWS operating income grew about 64% to $16.6B on 37% sales growth, and about 42% for the six months on 33% sales growth, showing positive operating leverage despite a near-doubling of AWS depreciation.
Consolidated operating income rose to $27.5B from $19.2B (+43%) on 20% sales growth, with sales and marketing and G&A shrinking as a percent of sales.

Contracted AWS backlog of about $496B with a 6.4-year weighted-average remaining life, anchored by multi-year OpenAI and Anthropic expansions, gives multi-year demand visibility; management says capacity will not meet demand through 2027.
Operating cash flow rose to $161.4B on a trailing basis (about +33%), so negative free cash flow is the product of front-loaded, demand-backed capex rather than weak core cash generation.

Custom silicon (Trainium and Graviton) and AWS AI are reported to be crossing $25B run rates each, with chip performance embedded in long-dated customer contracts, which could give Amazon a durable cost advantage in AI compute.
Retail is improving: North America sales grew 16% and International 15%, supported by advertising and unit sales.
bear_case: Trailing free cash flow swung to $(7.6)B from +$18.2B as net property and equipment purchases hit $169.0B; external financing of $75.2B over the twelve months is covering the gap.

Capex is still rising: Q2 cash capex was $53.1B versus $31.4B, 2026 capex guidance reportedly rose to $220B, and unpaid property and equipment purchases jumped to about $29.3B in the first half, implying more cash outflow ahead.

The AWS margin print may flatter reality. AWS net additions were $48.6B in Q2 versus only a $3.2B increase in AWS D&A, so much of the spend has yet to hit the P&L; Q3 consensus already reflects higher depreciation and a Prime Day shift.

Backlog quality is concentrated: two AI labs account for most of the recent growth, recognition depends on usage and chip performance, and those customers are partly funded by Amazon's own equity stakes, creating circularity.

Reported net income of $62.6B was inflated by $53.4B of non-operating gains tied to private AI investments, which are valued partly with Level 3 inputs and could reverse; tax provision also jumped to $18.2B.

Debt is rising to fund the build-out: large multi-currency note issuance, a $17.5B term loan, Q2 interest expense of $1.3B versus $0.5B, and commitments of about $650B versus $387B reduce flexibility.
Q3 revenue guidance was reportedly below Street expectations, and persistent AWS competitive-gap concerns versus Microsoft and Google keep the stock sensitive to any growth slowdown.

what_to_watch.text:
**Free Cash Flow and Capex Funding:** Trailing free cash flow fell to $(7.6) billion from +$18.2 billion as net property and equipment purchases rose to $169.0 billion against operating cash flow of $161.4 billion, and financing inflows of $75.2 billion covered the gap. Property and equipment acquired but not yet paid also jumped to about $29.3 billion in the first half, suggesting reported capex understates near-term cash needs. That said, operating cash flow grew roughly 33%, and the capex is aimed at capacity that management says is still short of demand.

-> Monitor trailing free cash flow, the unpaid property and equipment liability, and any change to the 2026 capex outlook (reportedly raised to $220 billion).

**AWS Growth Durability:** AWS sales rose 37% in Q2 2026 to $42.2 billion (33% for the first half), and backlog reportedly reached about $496 billion with a 6.4-year weighted-average life. Management has said capacity will fall short of demand through 2027, supporting continued acceleration. However, recognition depends on customer usage and delivery, and the growth comparison gets tougher from here.

-> Monitor whether AWS growth holds at or above roughly 30%, plus the sequential change in backlog and how much converts to revenue.

**AWS Margin vs. Depreciation Lag:** AWS operating income rose about 64% to $16.6 billion on 37% sales growth, indicating strong incremental margins even as AWS D&A rose about 67% to $8.1 billion. However, Q2 AWS net additions to property and equipment of $48.6 billion (versus $16.0 billion) have barely begun to depreciate, so a rough six-year life implies a step-up in quarterly D&A as assets enter service. Analysts also cite higher depreciation as a drag on expected EPS growth.

-> Monitor AWS operating income and implied margin, AWS D&A growth, and management commentary on the timing of assets placed in service.

**Backlog Concentration and AI Equity Stakes:** Backlog growth of about $252 billion in the first half is largely tied to the OpenAI ($100 billion over 8 years) and Anthropic (more than $100 billion over 10 years) expansions, both including obligations tied to AWS chip performance. Private-company equity investments carried at $122.3 billion (from $16.2 billion) drove $53.4 billion of Q2 other income, and the remaining $21.3 billion OpenAI commitment was funded after quarter-end. On the other hand, the multi-year terms and chip integration make the commitments sticky, and the long 6.4-year weighted life adds visibility.

-> Monitor non-operating gains or losses in other income, further equity funding of AI partners, and any disclosure on customer concentration within backlog.

**Debt, Interest Cost, and Liquidity:** Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were flat at about $123.0 billion while Amazon issued large USD, EUR, CHF, and CAD notes and signed a $17.5 billion undrawn delayed-draw term loan. Q2 interest expense rose to $1.3 billion from $0.5 billion, and total commitments are reported at about $650 billion versus $387 billion. That said, the term loan is undrawn and interest income of $1.3 billion offsets part of the cost.

-> Monitor interest expense, any drawdown of the term loan, new debt issuance, and the cash and marketable securities balance.

**Q3 Guide and Consolidated Margin:** Q3 2026 net sales guidance is reported at $197-202 billion (about 9-12% growth) with consensus EPS near $2.03, a sharp slowdown from Q2's 20% growth, partly reflecting the Prime Day shift. Operating income rose 43% in Q2 to $27.5 billion, and retail margins benefited from lower sales and marketing and G&A as a share of sales. However, Q2 sales were boosted by timing effects and depreciation is set to climb, so margin upside may be harder to sustain.

-> Monitor reported net sales against the $197-202 billion range, consolidated operating income, and the fourth-quarter guide.

**Custom Silicon as a Second Profit Pool:** Reports indicate that both AWS AI and the Trainium/Graviton chip business crossed $25 billion annual run rates in Q2 2026, growing at triple-digit rates, with Graviton commitments reportedly up nearly 3x sequentially. The filing shows chip performance embedded in the OpenAI and Anthropic obligations, but it does not break out chip revenue, and the run-rate figures come from secondary sources. That said, if chips lower unit compute cost, they could partly offset depreciation pressure.

-> Monitor any disclosure of chip or AI run rates, Trainium commitments, and commentary on cost per unit of compute.

**Earnings Quality and Non-Operating Items:** Q2 net income of $62.6 billion (diluted EPS $5.75) sat far above operating income of $27.5 billion because Other income (expense), net was $53.4 billion, offset by an $18.2 billion tax provision. Such gains reflect mark-ups of private investments and are not repeatable at this scale. However, operating income itself grew 43%, so the core business is improving independent of these gains.

-> Monitor the split between operating income and non-operating gains in the Q3 results, and compare EPS on an operating basis to consensus.

data_gaps: Total debt or long-term debt balances were not included in the provided filing excerpts, so a total debt figure could not be extracted.

A stand-alone Q2 2026 free cash flow figure was not provided in the filing excerpts; only the trailing-twelve-month reconciliation was available.
The filing excerpts do not disclose how much of the new AWS capex is still in construction or the depreciation schedule, so the timing of the depreciation step-up cannot be sized from the filing.
Chip (Trainium/Graviton) revenue is not broken out in the filing excerpts; run-rate figures come only from secondary news coverage.
